assumptions.condition: The law \(P\) of \(X\) is jointly centered Gaussian.

novel.justification: Joint Gaussianity is an explicitly restrictive component of the maintained covariance-based subclass. It makes the observed second moments determine the maintained law and makes zero cross-covariance equivalent to independence of the coordinate disturbance stacks. It is plausible for coordinate-aligned repeated measurements with Gaussian shared shocks and readout noise, but excludes the broader non-Gaussian LiMVAM families used by several comparators.

assumptions.condition: For each \(a\in M\), \(X^{(a)}=B^{0,(a)}X^{(a)}+\varepsilon^{(a)}\) almost surely under \(P\).
For all distinct \(i,j\in V\) and all \(a,b\in M\), \(\operatorname{Cov}_P(\varepsilon_i^{(a)},\varepsilon_j^{(b)})=0\).

novel.justification: This component-alignment restriction says that cross-view dependence is carried only by disturbances with the same variable label. Under joint Gaussianity it is equivalent to mutual independence of the stacked vectors \((\varepsilon_i^{(a)})_{a\in M}\) across distinct \(i\), and, for any candidate order, it is exactly the structural restriction represented by diagonal residual cross-blocks. The concrete mechanism \(\varepsilon_i^{(a)}=\lambda_{ia}U_i+\eta_i^{(a)}\) in \(\text{def:coordinate-sensor-mechanism}\) realizes it for coordinate-aligned repeated sensors with coordinate-specific shared shocks and independent readout noise; it is not asserted for arbitrary multimodal or neuroimaging measurements.

Positive definiteness places every stacked coordinate disturbance in the interior of the covariance cone and supports the inverse operations and full-view completion certificates. In the repeated-sensor mechanism, \(\Gamma_i=\operatorname{Var}(U_i)\lambda_i\lambda_i^{\mathsf T}+\operatorname{diag}_{a\in M}\operatorname{Var}(\eta_i^{(a)})\succ0\) because every readout-noise variance is positive. Singular shared-noise limits are outside the theorem.

assumptions.condition: The \(n_S\) aligned calibration vectors form an independent and identically distributed sample from the \(S\)-marginal of \(P\).

novel.justification: This is the aligned component of a novel calibration-plus-marginals sampling design. It is realistic for a designated repeated-measurement calibration cohort drawn from the same target population, but excludes signal-dependent enrollment, selection, and transport from a different population.

assumptions.condition: For each \(a\in M\), the \(n_a\) available viewwise observations form an independent and identically distributed sample from the \(a\)-marginal of \(P\).

novel.justification: This is the marginal-retention component of the calibration-plus-marginals design: additional viewwise observations come from the same target population as the calibration cohort. No independence across covariance estimators is imposed; the calibration observations may be included in a view's marginal sample, and independence across sources is available only when cohorts are disjoint. Selection and transport are excluded.

This is a uniform away-from-feasibility-strata condition: every order excluded by the population moments has an observed residual off-diagonal bounded below by a preassigned tolerance. It is satisfied on compact families that avoid the finite union of wrong-order residual-equality varieties, including the explicit \(p=2,m=3\) strictness witness with its unequal \(1/5\) versus \(2/5\) disturbance correlation. The margin can be assessed by simultaneous lower confidence bounds for the finitely many residual scores.

This is a uniform away-from-support-strata condition: each ancestry relation common to the compatible tuples has, in every tuple, at least one directed path whose coefficient product exceeds a preassigned tolerance. It holds for compact coefficient families with a common ancestral path whose edge magnitudes are bounded away from zero, such as finite-view chains with all active edges in \([c,C]\) for fixed \(c>0\). It is empirically interpretable through simultaneous lower confidence bounds on the finitely many candidate path products.

definitions.name: \(\mathfrak M_{p,m}^{\mathrm{CA}}\)
definitions.construction: \(\mathfrak M_{p,m}^{\mathrm{CA}}=\{(P,B^0,\varepsilon,\Gamma,\pi_0):p\ge2,\ m\ge2,\ (P,B^0,\varepsilon,\Gamma,\pi_0)\text{ satisfies every member property listed below}\}\).

definitions.name: Coordinate-aligned repeated-sensor mechanism
definitions.construction: For every \(i\in V\), let \(U_i\) be centered Gaussian, and for every \(i\in V\) and \(a\in M\), let \(\eta_i^{(a)}\) be centered Gaussian with \(\operatorname{Var}(\eta_i^{(a)})>0\). Require the variables \((U_i)_{i\in V}\) to be mutually independent, the variables \((\eta_i^{(a)})_{i\in V,a\in M}\) to be mutually independent, and the two families to be independent. For deterministic loadings \(\lambda_{ia}\), set \(\varepsilon_i^{(a)}=\lambda_{ia}U_i+\eta_i^{(a)}\). Then the coordinate stacks are mutually independent and \(\Gamma_i=\operatorname{Var}(U_i)\lambda_i\lambda_i^{\mathsf T}+\operatorname{diag}_{a\in M}\operatorname{Var}(\eta_i^{(a)})\succ0\), where \(\lambda_i=(\lambda_{ia})_{a\in M}\).

definitions.name: \(P_{\mathrm{ex}}\)
definitions.construction: Set \(p=2\), \(m=3\), and \(M=\{1,2,3\}\). Let \((\varepsilon_1^{(a)})_{a\in M}\) and \((\varepsilon_2^{(a)})_{a\in M}\) be independent centered Gaussian vectors with covariance matrices \(\Gamma_1=\begin{pmatrix}1&1/5&1/5\\1/5&1&1/5\\1/5&1/5&1\end{pmatrix}\) and \(\Gamma_2=\begin{pmatrix}1&1/5&2/5\\1/5&1&1/5\\2/5&1/5&1\end{pmatrix}\), respectively. For each \(a\in M\), set \(X_1^{(a)}=\varepsilon_1^{(a)}\) and \(X_2^{(a)}=X_1^{(a)}+\varepsilon_2^{(a)}\), and let \(P_{\mathrm{ex}}\) be the resulting law. Thus \(B^{0,(a)}=\begin{pmatrix}0&0\\1&0\end{pmatrix}\) and \(\Sigma^{aa}=\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\1&2\end{pmatrix}\) in every view.

definitions.name: \(B_\pi\)
definitions.construction: For each \(a\in M\) and \(k=1,\ldots,p\), set \(B_\pi^{(a)}[\pi(k),\pi(1{:}k-1)]=\Sigma^{aa}[\pi(k),\pi(1{:}k-1)]\{\Sigma^{aa}[\pi(1{:}k-1),\pi(1{:}k-1)]\}^{-1}\), set all other entries in that row to zero, and set \(L_\pi^{(a)}=I_p-B_\pi^{(a)}\).

definitions.name: \(R_\pi\)
definitions.construction: For \(a,b\in M\), \(R_\pi^{ab}=L_\pi^{(a)}\Sigma^{ab}(L_\pi^{(b)})^{\mathsf T}\).

definitions.name: \(d_\pi,d_*,\Pi_S^{(\tau)},\Theta_S^{(\tau)}\)
definitions.construction: For each \(\pi\in\mathfrak S_V\), define \(d_\pi=\max_{a\ne b\in S,\,i\ne j\in V}|R_\pi^{ab}[i,j]|/\sqrt{R_\pi^{aa}[i,i]R_\pi^{bb}[j,j]}\) and \(d_*=\min_{\pi\in\mathfrak S_V}d_\pi\). For \(\tau\ge0\), define \(\Pi_S^{(\tau)}=\{\pi\in\mathfrak S_V:d_\pi\le\tau\}\) and \(\Theta_S^{(\tau)}=\{T_\pi:\pi\in\Pi_S^{(\tau)}\}\), with numerical duplicates removed. The case \(\tau=0\) equals the maintained exact compatibility objects.

definitions.name: \(\Gamma_\pi\)
definitions.construction: For each \(j\in V\), set \(\Gamma_{\pi,j}[a,b]=R_\pi^{ab}[j,j]\) when \(a,b\in S\), set \(\Gamma_{\pi,j}[a,a]=R_\pi^{aa}[j,j]\) when \(a\in M\setminus S\), and set every other entry involving an unselected view to zero.

definitions.name: \(\Pi_S(\mathcal O_S)\)
definitions.construction: \(\Pi_S(\mathcal O_S)=\{\pi\in\mathfrak S_V:\operatorname{offdiag}(R_\pi^{ab})=0\ \text{for every distinct }a,b\in S\}\).

definitions.name: \(\Theta_S(\mathcal O_S)\)
definitions.construction: \(\Theta_S(\mathcal O_S)=\{T_\pi=(B_\pi^{(a)})_{a\in M}:\pi\in\Pi_S(\mathcal O_S)\}\), where braces remove numerical duplicates.

definitions.name: \(Z_A\)
definitions.construction: For \(U_A=V\setminus A\), define \(Z_A^{(a)}=X_{U_A}^{(a)}-\Sigma^{aa}[U_A,A]\{\Sigma^{aa}[A,A]\}^{-1}X_A^{(a)}\), with \(Z_\varnothing^{(a)}=X^{(a)}\).

definitions.name: \(C_A\)
definitions.construction: Set \(C_A^{ab}=\operatorname{Cov}_P(Z_A^{(a)},Z_A^{(b)})\) for every observed pair \(a=b\in M\) or \(a,b\in S\).

definitions.name: \(q_{A,r,t}^{ab}\)
definitions.construction: For \(r,t\in U_A\), \(r\ne t\), and distinct \(a,b\in S\), define \(q_{A,r,t}^{ab}=C_A^{ab}[r,t]-C_A^{ab}[r,r]\,C_A^{bb}[r,r]^{-1}C_A^{bb}[r,t]\); call \(r\) removable at \(A\) exactly when every such score is zero.

definitions.name: \(\mathcal D_S\)
definitions.construction: Starting at \(\varnothing\), create one vertex for each reachable \(A\subseteq V\) and an edge \(A\to A\cup\{r\}\) precisely when \(r\in U_A\) is removable according to \(q_A\); memoize each \(C_A\) once.

definitions.name: \(\prec_S\)
definitions.construction: For distinct \(i,j\in V\), define \(i\prec_S j\) exactly when \(G_T\) contains a directed path from \(i\) to \(j\) for every \(T\in\Theta_S(\mathcal O_S)\).

definitions.name: \(W_\pi\)
definitions.construction: Under the full moment collection \(\mathcal O_M\), define \(W_\pi=\{\{a,b\}\in\binom M2:\operatorname{offdiag}(R_\pi^{ab})\ne0\}\).

definitions.name: \(S_{\min}\)
definitions.construction: Choose \(S_{\min}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{H\subseteq M,\,\lvert H\rvert\ge2}\{\lvert H\rvert:\Theta_H(\mathcal O_H)=\Theta_M(\mathcal O_M)\}\), with lexicographic tie breaking.

definitions.name: \(\mathcal C_n(\alpha)\)
definitions.construction: When \(\eta_{S,n}<1\) and every \(\eta_{a,n}<1\), set \(r_{S,n}(\alpha)=((1-\eta_{S,n})^{-2}-1)\lVert\widehat\Sigma_{\mathrm{pair}}^{SS}\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}\) and \(r_{a,n}(\alpha)=((1-\eta_{a,n})^{-2}-1)\lVert\widehat\Sigma_{\mathrm{marg}}^{aa}\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}\). Define \(\mathcal C_n(\alpha)=\{\mathcal O'_S:\lVert\Sigma'^{SS}-\widehat\Sigma_{\mathrm{pair}}^{SS}\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}\le r_{S,n}(\alpha),\ \lVert\Sigma'^{aa}-\widehat\Sigma_{\mathrm{marg}}^{aa}\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}\le r_{a,n}(\alpha)\ \text{for every }a\in M,\ \Sigma'^{SS}\succ0,\ \Sigma'^{aa}\succ0\}\), where \(\eta_{S,n}=\sqrt{d_S/n_S}+\sqrt{2\log(2K_{\mathrm{obs}}/\alpha)/n_S}\) and \(\eta_{a,n}=\sqrt{p/n_a}+\sqrt{2\log(2K_{\mathrm{obs}}/\alpha)/n_a}\).

definitions.name: \(\widehat\Theta_{S,n}(\alpha)\)
definitions.construction: \(\widehat\Theta_{S,n}(\alpha)=\bigcup_{\mathcal O'_S\in\mathcal C_n(\alpha)}\Theta_S(\mathcal O'_S)\), and \(\widehat\prec_{S,n}(\alpha)\) is ancestry common to every tuple in this union.

definitions.name: \(\delta_{\mathrm{feas}}\)
definitions.construction: \(\delta_{\mathrm{feas}}(\mathcal O_S)=\min_{\pi\notin\Pi_S(\mathcal O_S)}\max_{\{a,b\}\in\binom S2}\|\operatorname{offdiag}(R_\pi^{ab})\|_{\max}\), with the minimum of the empty set equal to \(+\infty\).

definitions.name: \(\delta_{\mathrm{path}}\)
definitions.construction: Define \(\delta_{\mathrm{path}}(\mathcal O_S)=\min_{T\in\Theta_S(\mathcal O_S),\,i\prec_S j}\max_{g:i=v_0\to\cdots\to v_\ell=j\text{ in }G_T}\prod_{h=1}^{\ell}\max_{a\in M}|B_{v_hv_{h-1}}^{(a)}|\), with an empty minimum equal to \(+\infty\).

definitions.name: \(\omega_{\mathrm{feas}},\omega_{\mathrm{path}}\)
definitions.construction: For observed collections \(\mathcal O_S\) and \(\mathcal O'_S\), set \(d_{\mathrm{obs}}(\mathcal O_S,\mathcal O'_S)=\max\{\max_{a\in M}\|\Sigma^{aa}-\Sigma'^{aa}\|_{\mathrm{op}},\max_{a,b\in S}\|\Sigma^{ab}-\Sigma'^{ab}\|_{\mathrm{op}}\}\); for coefficient tuples set \(d_{\mathrm{coef}}(T,T')=\max_{a\in M}\|B^{(a)}-B'^{(a)}\|_{\mathrm{op}}\). At \(\mathcal O_S\), define \(\lambda_*=\min_{a\in M}\lambda_{\min}(\Sigma^{aa})\), \(K_*=\max\{1,\max_{a\in M}\|\Sigma^{aa}\|_{\mathrm{op}},\max_{a,b\in S}\|\Sigma^{ab}\|_{\mathrm{op}}\}\), \(L_B=2\sqrt p(\lambda_*^{-1}+K_*\lambda_*^{-2})\), \(G_*=1+\sqrt p(1+2K_*/\lambda_*)\), \(L_R=G_*^2+L_BG_*(2K_*+\lambda_*/2)\), \(K_B=\max\{1,\max_{\pi\in\mathfrak S_V,\,a\in M}\|B_\pi^{(a)}\|_{\max}\}\), and \(L_{\mathrm{path}}=(p-1)(K_B+1)^{p-2}\). For \(0\le u\le\min\{\lambda_*/2,L_B^{-1}\}\), set \(\omega_{\mathrm{feas}}(u)=L_Ru\) and \(\omega_{\mathrm{path}}(u)=L_{\mathrm{path}}L_Bu\). Finally set \(\bar r_n(\alpha)=\max\{r_{S,n}(\alpha),\max_{a\in M}r_{a,n}(\alpha)\}\).

definitions.name: \(\Omega_{\pi_0}^{\mathrm{CA}}\)
definitions.construction: For fixed \(p\ge2\), \(m\ge3\), and \(\pi_0\in\mathfrak S_V\), define \(\Omega_{\pi_0}^{\mathrm{CA}}=\{\theta=((B^{(a)})_{a\in M},(\Gamma_i)_{i\in V}):B^{(a)}[\pi_0(k),\pi_0(j)]=0\text{ whenever }j\ge k,\ \Gamma_i\in\mathbb S_{++}^{m}\text{ for every }a\in M,i\in V\}\). Give this set the relative Euclidean topology on the free strictly \(\pi_0\)-lower-triangular coefficients and symmetric covariance entries. Each \(\theta\) induces \(\Sigma_\theta^{ab}=(I_p-B^{(a)})^{-1}\operatorname{diag}_{i\in V}(\Gamma_i[a,b])(I_p-B^{(b)})^{-\mathsf T}\), hence a centered component-aligned Gaussian law.

e\pi_0\), express each off-diagonal entry \(R_\pi^{ab}(	heta)[i,j]\), \(i

Denote the resulting polynomial numerator by \(f_{\pi,ij}^{ab}(	heta)\), set \(F_\pi^{ab}(	heta)=\sum_{i
e j}f_{\pi,ij}^{ab}(	heta)^2\), and define \(\mathcal E_{ab,\pi_0}=\{	heta\in\Omega_{\pi_0}^{\mathrm{CA}}:\prod_{\pi
e\pi_0}F_\pi^{ab}(	heta)=0\}\).

definitions.name: \(\theta_\pi^{ab}\)
definitions.construction: For a fixed \(\pi\ne\pi_0\), choose \(u,v\in V\) with \(u\) preceding \(v\) under \(\pi_0\) and \(v\) preceding \(u\) under \(\pi\). Choose \(\beta\ne0\) and distinct \(r_u,r_v\in(-1,1)\). Set the only nonzero structural coefficient to \(B^{(a)}[v,u]=B^{(b)}[v,u]=\beta\), with every coefficient in the other views zero. Set every within-view disturbance variance to one, set \(\Gamma_u[a,b]=r_u\), \(\Gamma_v[a,b]=r_v\), complete these two matrices by symmetry and zero off-pair entries, and set \(\Gamma_i=I_m\) for every other coordinate. Call the resulting parameter \(\theta_\pi^{ab}\).

definitions.name: Quotient-enumeration handle
definitions.construction: Start from the acyclic removed-set representation \(\mathcal D_S\). Test whether equality of completed modified-Cholesky tuples admits a locally compositional edge coloring in a decomposable AND--OR representation; if local compositionality fails, use the lexicographically first coefficient-changing removable transition as the starting move for a reverse-search parent and derive its child oracle from reachable removed-set states.

statements.statement: Fix \(\mathcal O_S\) generated by at least one member of \(\mathfrak M_{p,m}^{\mathrm{CA}}\). Joint Gaussianity and component alignment imply that the stacked disturbance vectors \((\varepsilon_i^{(a)})_{a\in M}\) are mutually independent across \(i\in V\). For every permutation \(\pi\), there exists a full joint component-aligned Gaussian completion with common order \(\pi\) and observed moments \(\mathcal O_S\) if and only if \(\operatorname{offdiag}(R_\pi^{ab})=0\) for every distinct \(a,b\in S\). When this holds, the structural coefficients are uniquely \(T_\pi\), each selected disturbance block \((R_\pi^{ab}[j,j])_{a,b\in S}\) is positive definite, and every \(\Gamma_{\pi,j}\) is a full positive-definite noise certificate. Consequently, \(\Theta_S(\mathcal O_S)\) is the complete coefficient equivalence class within \(\mathfrak M_{p,m}^{\mathrm{CA}}\).
statements.justification: This supporting lemma supplies the fixed-order observable criterion and positive-definite completion used by the generic theorem and the complete-set algorithms.
statements.gap: Section 4.6 of HeurtebiseEtAl2026LiMVAM is point-identifying under full pairing and its diversity assumption; this lemma instead records the orderwise residual characterization needed for selected pairing on the narrower component-aligned subclass, without treating that characterization as the principal novelty.
statements.consumer: For coordinate-aligned repeated measurements satisfying the maintained mechanism, an analyst can determine exactly which shared orders and view-specific coefficient matrices remain licensed when only a calibration subset is aligned.

statements.statement:
Fix \(p\ge2\), \(m\ge3\), a common order \(\pi_0\), and any preassigned distinct views \(a,b\in M\). On \(\Omega_{\pi_0}^{\mathrm{CA}}\), no edge-minimality condition and no diversity condition from Assumption 2 of HeurtebiseEtAl2026LiMVAM is imposed. For every \(\pi
e\pi_0\), all entries of \(\operatorname{offdiag}(R_\pi^{ab}(	heta))\) are rational functions whose denominators are positive products of principal minors, and the denominator-cleared polynomial \(F_\pi^{ab}\) is not identically zero. More precisely, the witness \(	heta_\pi^{ab}\in\Omega_{\pi_0}^{\mathrm{CA}}\) has a wrong-order residual entry equal, up to transpose orientation, to \( eta(r_u-r_v)/(1+ eta^2)
e0\). Therefore \(\mathcal E_{ab,\pi_0}=\{	heta:\prod_{\pi
e\pi_0}F_\pi^{ab}(	heta)=0\}\) is a proper algebraic subset of \(\Omega_{\pi_0}^{\mathrm{CA}}\). For every \(	heta\in\Omega_{\pi_0}^{\mathrm{CA}}\setminus\mathcal E_{ab,\pi_0}\), \(\Pi_{\{a,b\}}(\mathcal O_{\{a,b\}})=\{\pi_0\}\) and \(\Theta_{\{a,b\}}(\mathcal O_{\{a,b\}})=\Theta_M(\mathcal O_M)=\{T_{\pi_0}\}\). Hence every preassigned view pair is generically sufficient and \(\lvert S_{\min}vert=2\) under the maintained convention \(\lvert Svert\ge2\). The exceptional set has Lebesgue measure zero in the relative Euclidean parameter space and is avoided almost surely by every parameter law absolutely continuous with respect to that Lebesgue measure.
statements.justification: The theorem shows that two aligned views, chosen before seeing the parameters, generically recover the full-view coefficient tuple and that all failures are confined to an explicit algebraic equality locus.
statements.gap: HeurtebiseEtAl2026LiMVAM, Section 4.6, Assumption 2 and Theorem 3 obtain full-pair point identification from edgewise cross-view correlation diversity. On a narrower component-aligned Gaussian class, this theorem removes that diversity assumption, fixes an arbitrary pair in advance, and proves generic full-information equivalence by a nonvanishing polynomial for every wrong order; this is a different observation-regime result, not a containment claim for their published class.
statements.consumer: A coordinate-aligned repeated-sensor study can preassign any two views for paired calibration and retain all remaining views only marginally, with failures localized to a testable finite family of algebraic equalities.

statements.statement: The law \(P_{\mathrm{ex}}\) in \(\text{def:strictness-example}\), together with its displayed coefficients, disturbances, covariance matrices, and order \((1,2)\), belongs to \(\mathfrak M_{2,3}^{\mathrm{CA}}\). Let \(H=\{1,2\}\subsetneq M=\{1,2,3\}\). The two orders \((1,2)\) and \((2,1)\) are both compatible with \(\mathcal O_H\), and \(\Theta_H(\mathcal O_H)=\{(\begin{psmallmatrix}0&0\\1&0\end{psmallmatrix})_{a\in M},(\begin{psmallmatrix}0&1/2\\0&0\end{psmallmatrix})_{a\in M}\}\). Under full calibration, \(\Theta_M(\mathcal O_M)=\{(\begin{psmallmatrix}0&0\\1&0\end{psmallmatrix})_{a\in M}\}\). The displayed structural parameter lies in \(\mathcal E_{12,(1,2)}\): the reverse-order residual restriction vanishes for the calibrated pair because \(\Gamma_1[1,2]=\Gamma_2[1,2]=1/5\), but fails for the observed full-pair block \(\{1,3\}\) because \(\Gamma_1[1,3]=1/5\ne2/5=\Gamma_2[1,3]\).
statements.justification: The numerical witness proves strict enlargement from full to partial calibration within the component-aligned subclass.
statements.gap: Theorem 3 of HeurtebiseEtAl2026LiMVAM treats full pairing under Assumption 2 and supplies no proper-subset example; this proposition isolates a two-variable, three-view law inside the narrower maintained class whose coefficient set expands numerically when one calibration view is removed.
statements.consumer: Calibration designers obtain a concrete failure certificate showing why a proper view pair can be insufficient even though the fully paired cohort identifies one tuple.

statements.statement: For every \(A\subseteq V\), the state \(C_A\) equals covariance after orthogonal projection on the span of the coordinates indexed by \(A\) and is independent of the order in which \(A\) was removed. A permutation \(\pi\) belongs to \(\Pi_S(\mathcal O_S)\) if and only if \(\pi(k)\) is removable at \(A_{k-1}=\{\pi(1),\ldots,\pi(k-1)\}\) for every \(k\). Thus source-to-sink paths in \(\mathcal D_S\) are in bijection with compatible orders, and all states and removable edges can be constructed in \(O(\operatorname{poly}(p,m)2^p)\) exact-real arithmetic operations and \(O(\operatorname{poly}(p,m)2^p)\) memory.
statements.justification: Path independence is the step that replaces factorial order search by a memoized subset-state representation.
statements.gap: Section 3.1 of DirectLiNGAM identifies one exogenous variable in Lemma 1, closes the non-Gaussian LiNGAM model after removing that true root in Lemma 2, and preserves the remaining causal order in Corollary 1. The recursive proof supporting Section 4.6 of HeurtebiseEtAl2026LiMVAM likewise follows roots licensed by its diversity score. Neither source proves that all sequential projections reaching the same removed set have an identical covariance state, nor gives necessary-and-sufficient steps whose complete source-to-sink paths are exactly all compatible orders. GhoshalHonorio2018LinearSEM uses a Schur update in a different point-identified sink model.
statements.consumer: The subset DAG supplies a complete feasibility oracle and the finite state space required by quotient enumeration and calibration design.

statements.statement: Let \(p=2\), let the true common order be \((1,2)\), and consider calibrated views \(a,b\) with the same nonzero structural edge coefficient and equal positive within-view disturbance variances variable by variable. The reverse order \((2,1)\) is compatible if and only if \(\rho_1^{ab}=\rho_2^{ab}\). Hence unequal disturbance correlations reject the reverse order, while equal correlations reproduce the homogeneous two-view Gaussian ambiguity.
statements.justification: The reduction is a falsifiable sanity check and identifies the exact equality boundary in the smallest system.
statements.gap: HeurtebiseEtAl2026LiMVAM supplies a diversity condition for recovery but not this pointwise reverse-order equivalence calculation under partial calibration.
statements.consumer: The formula gives practitioners a transparent diagnostic for whether two calibrated views contain any directional information.

statements.statement: For any \(H\subseteq M\) with \(\lvert H\rvert\ge2\), \(\Theta_H(\mathcal O_H)=\Theta_M(\mathcal O_M)\) if and only if, for every permutation \(\pi\) whose tuple \(T_\pi\) does not belong to \(\Theta_M(\mathcal O_M)\), the induced pair set \(\binom H2\) intersects \(W_\pi\). Therefore \(S_{\min}\) is exactly a minimum-cardinality induced-view hitting set for the coefficient-new residual-witness family. Exhaustive subset search together with \(\mathcal D_H\) gives a finite exact certificate of sufficiency and a surviving coefficient-new tuple for every smaller subset; if \(\Theta_M(\mathcal O_M)\) is a singleton, \(S_{\min}\) identifies the full coefficient tuple for every view from its marginal covariance.
statements.justification: This computational corollary rewrites tuple preservation as an exact residual-witness certificate while respecting numerical duplicates; it is supporting infrastructure rather than the novelty kernel.
statements.gap: HauserBuhlmann2014ActiveLearning and LindgrenEtAl2018CostAware motivate separator-based acquisition, while this direct consequence of the compatibility lemma records the passive residual-witness implementation needed here.
statements.consumer: A coordinate-aligned repeated-sensor study can certify the smallest jointly calibrated view subset while retaining every viewwise series for marginal coefficient estimation.

statements.statement: The relation \(\prec_S\) is a strict partial order and equals the ancestral relations shared by every full joint component-aligned Gaussian completion of \(\mathcal O_S\). It is computable by intersecting transitive closures of the union support graphs \(G_T\) over distinct \(T\in\Theta_S(\mathcal O_S)\), so it is invariant to duplicate inducing orders.
statements.justification: The poset reports the causal ordering content that is identified even when the full order is not.
statements.gap: The full-pair anchor targets a recovered order; no cited result extracts the invariant ancestral content of a partial-calibration coefficient set.
statements.consumer: Downstream pathway analyses can restrict claims to ancestral relations shared by all compatible view-specific repeated-measurement mechanisms.

statements.statement: Under the Gaussian calibration and marginal sampling conditions, whenever \(\eta_{S,n}<1\) and every \(\eta_{a,n}<1\), the explicit radii in \(\mathcal C_n(\alpha)\) satisfy \(\Pr\{\mathcal O_S\in\mathcal C_n(\alpha)\}\ge1-\alpha\), and on this event \(\Theta_S(\mathcal O_S)\subseteq\widehat\Theta_{S,n}(\alpha)\). More explicitly, for any positive-definite \(\mathcal O'_S\) with \(u=d_{\mathrm{obs}}(\mathcal O_S,\mathcal O'_S)\le\min\{\lambda_*/2,L_B^{-1}\}\), every order and observed view pair obey \(\|B_\pi^{(a)}(\mathcal O'_S)-B_\pi^{(a)}(\mathcal O_S)\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le L_Bu\) and \(\|R_\pi^{ab}(\mathcal O'_S)-R_\pi^{ab}(\mathcal O_S)\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le\omega_{\mathrm{feas}}(u)=L_Ru\); every corresponding directed-path product changes by at most \(\omega_{\mathrm{path}}(u)=L_{\mathrm{path}}L_Bu\). Hence, if \(\omega_{\mathrm{feas}}(u)\le\kappa_{\mathrm{feas}}/2\), then \(\Pi_S(\mathcal O'_S)\subseteq\Pi_S(\mathcal O_S)\). On the coverage event, if \(2\bar r_n(\alpha)\le\min\{\lambda_*/2,L_B^{-1}\}\), \(\omega_{\mathrm{feas}}(2\bar r_n(\alpha))\le\kappa_{\mathrm{feas}}/2\), and \(\omega_{\mathrm{path}}(2\bar r_n(\alpha))\le\kappa_{\mathrm{path}}/2\), then the Hausdorff distance induced by \(d_{\mathrm{coef}}\) from \(\widehat\Theta_{S,n}(\alpha)\) to \(\Theta_S(\mathcal O_S)\) is at most \(2L_B\bar r_n(\alpha)\), and \(\widehat\prec_{S,n}(\alpha)=\prec_S\). Consequently, if \(\min(n_S,\min_{a\in M}n_a)\to\infty\), the two novel margins are bounded below by \(\kappa_{\mathrm{feas}}>0\) and \(\kappa_{\mathrm{path}}>0\), and \(\alpha_n\to0\) with vanishing radii, then Hausdorff consistency and exact essential-poset recovery hold in probability.
statements.justification: Set inversion makes uncertainty honest when the population output is non-singleton, while the explicit moduli translate covariance error into branch and ancestral-path stability.
statements.gap: ChernozhukovHongTamer2007SetInference gives general contour inversion, while GhoshalHonorio2018LinearSEM uses precision-diagonal and nonzero-precision-entry gaps for one recursive graph. Neither source defines the wrong-order residual or common-ancestral path-product margins, nor derives the displayed LiMVAM covariance-to-margin moduli.
statements.consumer: A future Cam-CAN MEG or fMRI diagnostic analysis can report an uncertainty-aware sensitivity envelope only after checking common-target sampling and failing to reject the component-aligned repeated-sensor mechanism on observed calibration blocks.

statements.statement: Fix distinct \(a,b\in M\), set \(S=\{a,b\}\), and let \(\theta\in\Omega_{\pi_0}^{\mathrm{CA}}\setminus\mathcal E_{ab,\pi_0}\). Then the pairwise wrong-order feasibility margin \(\delta_{\mathrm{feas}}(\mathcal O_S)\) is strictly positive because there are finitely many wrong orders. Under the calibration-plus-marginals sampling conditions and fixed positive feasibility and path-product margins, the covariance-region inversion specializes to Hausdorff recovery of the singleton \(\{T_{\pi_0}\}\) and exact recovery of its induced ancestral poset in probability as the sourcewise sample sizes diverge and \(\alpha_n\to0\) with vanishing radii.
statements.justification: This corollary turns the population genericity statement into the existing uncertainty-aware singleton and ancestral recovery guarantee.
statements.gap: The cited full-pair LiMVAM theorem does not connect a preassigned two-view generic algebraic region to covariance-set inversion under partial calibration.
statements.consumer: A two-view calibration study obtains a direct population-to-sample recovery guarantee whenever its parameter lies off the explicit exceptional variety and its stability margins are bounded away from zero.

statements.statement: Using the quotient-enumeration handle, determine whether every distinct tuple in \(\Theta_S(\mathcal O_S)\) can be emitted exactly once, together with a canonical inducing order and positive-definite noise certificate, in total \(O(\operatorname{poly}(p,m)2^p+\operatorname{poly}(p,m)N_{\mathrm{out}})\) exact-real arithmetic operations or with polynomial delay, without visiting every compatible source-to-sink path in \(\mathcal D_S\); if this complexity is impossible in the stated oracle model, derive a matching obstruction.
statements.justification: This is the genuine unresolved step between a compact feasibility DAG and a duplicate-free complete output algorithm.
statements.gap: GuoPerkovic2021MinimalEffects uses graphical effect signatures, WienobstEtAl2023MECEnumeration outputs graph-distinct DAGs, and WangEtAl2023EquivalenceEnumeration requires a local colored AND--OR congruence not established for global numerical tuples.
statements.consumer: A complete partial-calibration solver can scale on sparse or degenerate systems where factorially many compatible orders encode only a few coefficient mechanisms.

sampling_model.design: A novel calibration-plus-marginals design: an aligned calibration sample supplies \(n_S\) joint observations for views in \(S\), and each view supplies a viewwise sample containing its calibration observations when available together with any additional observations from the same target population.
sampling_model.units: Observations are independent and identically distributed across units within each source. The calibration sample and every viewwise source have the corresponding marginal law of the same target \(P\); they need not be mutually independent because calibration units may also enter marginal estimators. Cross-source independence holds only for disjoint cohorts.
sampling_model.treatment: There is no treatment variable; the causal target is the shared-order structural coefficient family and its invariant ancestry.
sampling_model.overlap: Alignment is required only among views in \(S\); no cross-view block involving an unselected view is observed. Signal-dependent selection, population transport, and source-specific target laws are excluded.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Empirical covariance blocks are estimated from the aligned and viewwise samples without assuming independence across block estimators; modified-Cholesky regressions and Schur states are recomputed for each moment collection in the confidence region.

tldr: For any preassigned pair of views, two-view calibration generically identifies the common order and every view-specific coefficient matrix on the explicitly restrictive component-aligned Gaussian subclass. The failure locus is an explicit proper algebraic set: each wrong order supplies a denominator-cleared residual polynomial, and a single-edge unequal-correlation witness proves that polynomial is nonzero. Thus two views attain the full-calibration singleton outside a Lebesgue-null set without edge minimality or the diversity assumption used by Heurtebise et al. A fixed-order residual lemma, path-independent removed-set recursion, computational hitting-set corollary, and covariance-region inversion support the headline. Equality examples lie on the exceptional set, including a law with one full-calibration tuple but two tuples for the pair \(\{1,2\}\). Duplicate-free output-sensitive traversal remains the open-ended question.

project_justification.gap: Heurtebise et al.'s Section 4.6, Assumption 2 and Theorem 3 give full-pair identification under edgewise correlation diversity on their broader disturbance class. DirectLiNGAM Section 3.1, Lemmas 1--2 and Corollary 1 justify recursive removal of one true exogenous variable. Shimizu's JointLiNGAM, Chen et al.'s individual-structure method, and Ghassami et al.'s multi-domain procedure borrow information across datasets or domains through non-Gaussianity, shared-population components, or shared structure with domain heterogeneity. None proves that an arbitrary pair fixed in advance attains full-calibration identification generically on a component-aligned Gaussian parameter space, locates every failure on a proper algebraic variety, or characterizes all surviving orders on that variety.
project_justification.niche: On the component-aligned subclass, finite-dimensional Gaussianity makes every fixed-order coefficient family observable from marginal modified Cholesky factors, while selected paired cross-blocks provide exact order-dependent orthogonality equations. This separates marginal coefficient recovery from the scarce paired information needed only for order discrimination.
project_justification.fill: The headline theorem clears the positive principal-minor denominators of every wrong-order residual restriction, proves nonvanishing by an explicit single-edge witness, and concludes that any preassigned view pair gives the full-view singleton outside a Lebesgue-null algebraic set. Supporting results supply fixed-order completion, complete path-independent recursion, equality-locus examples, a computational calibration certificate, and covariance-region inversion with explicit local stability moduli.

related_work: HeurtebiseEtAl2026LiMVAM is the flagship model anchor. Its Section 4.6, Assumption 2 requires, for every union-graph edge, a view pair with nonzero within-view cause--effect correlation and unequal absolute cross-view correlations for the cause and effect disturbance; its Theorem 3 identifies the causal partial order and all view-specific coefficient matrices from full pairing, with Assumption 3 adding a unique total order. On the intersection of its standing assumptions and Assumption 2 with the narrower component-aligned subclass, its full-pair singleton agrees with \(\Theta_M(\mathcal O_M)\) and the induced partial order; this is a restricted-domain consistency comparison only. The headline addresses a different observation regime: on the narrower class, any pair fixed before observing parameters equals the full-calibration singleton off an explicit proper algebraic set, without imposing edge minimality or Heurtebise et al.'s diversity assumption. The fixed-order residual iff is supporting infrastructure, not the principal novelty. ShimizuEtAl2011DirectLiNGAM is the recursive-residual comparator: Section 3.1, Lemma 1 finds one exogenous variable by residual independence, Lemma 2 preserves LiNGAM after removing that true root, and Corollary 1 preserves the remaining order. It does not prove removed-set path independence across different valid paths or characterize all compatible roots and complete compatible orders. The recursive proof behind Heurtebise et al.'s Theorem 3 likewise follows roots licensed by its diversity score and lacks those complete-frontier steps. Shimizu2012JointLiNGAM pools residual-independence information across unpaired non-Gaussian groups with a shared order. ChenEtAl2024IndividualCausal identifies individual structures through shared population components and Shared ICA under non-Gaussianity or noise-variance diversity. GhassamiEtAl2018MultiDomain uses domain-wise heterogeneity and shared causal structure across separate datasets. Those mechanisms differ from selected paired covariance blocks and do not return an exact possibly non-singleton compatibility set on algebraic equality loci. HyttinenEberhardtHoyer2012Overlapping studies pair conditions for experimental total effects, not paired-view residual covariances. GuoPerkovic2021MinimalEffects, WienobstEtAl2023MECEnumeration, WangEtAl2023EquivalenceEnumeration, and AvisFukuda1996ReverseSearch inform the open quotient-enumeration question without establishing a local congruence for numerical coefficient tuples. HauserBuhlmann2014ActiveLearning and LindgrenEtAl2018CostAware motivate only the separator analogy behind the computational hitting-set corollary. GhoshalHonorio2018LinearSEM uses precision-based recursive gaps rather than the residual and path-product margins here. Vershynin2018HighDimensionalProbability supplies Gaussian covariance concentration, and ChernozhukovHongTamer2007SetInference supplies general set inversion. MohanPearl2021MissingData motivates the exclusion of selection and transport. TaylorEtAl2017CamCAN documents a future diagnostic use case but does not validate component alignment or common-target calibration sampling.
technical_internal_limitation: The generic theorem is relative to the fixed-order finite-dimensional parameterization and gives no uniform distance from \(\mathcal E_{ab,\pi_0}\); near that variety, finite-sample order recovery can be unstable. Equality examples are genuine points on the exceptional set. In particular, \(P_{\mathrm{ex}}\in\mathcal E_{12,(1,2)}\) has two tuples for \(S=\{1,2\}\) although full pairing leaves one. The \(2^p\)-state result counts exact-real arithmetic operations and does not by itself give polynomial bit complexity. Exact rational \(p=m=3\) enumeration agreed with dynamic-programming leaves for every admissible calibration subset. The desired exact-once output bound remains confined to \(\text{oeq:output-sensitive-quotient}\). At population moments, \(d_*>0\) falsifies the maintained class on observed calibration blocks. In samples, rejection is warranted only when a simultaneous lower confidence bound for \(d_*\) is positive; non-rejection is not validation and says nothing about unobserved pairs.
honest_scope: Generic two-view sufficiency, the proper algebraic exceptional set, fixed-order completion, the strictness witness, removed-set recursion, essential poset, local stability modulus, and covariance inversion are proof obligations on the component-aligned Gaussian subclass. The residual compatibility iff and calibration hitting-set iff are supporting consequences, not headline novelty. Genericity is relative to coefficients respecting a fixed \(\pi_0\) and positive-definite coordinate disturbance covariances; it neither supplies a uniform margin nor identifies points on \(\mathcal E_{ab,\pi_0}\). Joint Gaussianity and component alignment exclude broader LiMVAMs, and positive-definite \(\Gamma_i\) excludes singular shared-noise limits. The repeated-sensor mechanism applies only to coordinate-aligned measurements. Calibration-plus-marginals sampling is sourcewise independent and identically distributed from one target population but need not make covariance estimators independent; selection and transport remain outside the model. The comparison with Heurtebise et al. is restricted to the intersection with their standing assumptions and Assumption 2. For \(\tau>0\), \(\Pi_S^{(\tau)}\) and \(\Theta_S^{(\tau)}\) are sensitivity envelopes, not unrestricted-class identified sets. Cam-CAN MEG and fMRI remain future diagnostic use cases. Output-sensitive quotient enumeration remains open.
seeds: A generic two-view sufficiency theorem: every preassigned pair matches full calibration off an explicit proper algebraic exceptional set.
An output-sensitive quotient traversal of the removed-set order DAG that emits each distinct full-view coefficient tuple once.
A minimum-cardinality passive calibration design characterized by residual-witness hitting, including equality-stratum collapse.
Operator-norm covariance-region inversion with explicit covariance-to-margin moduli, Hausdorff coefficient-set consistency, and exact essential-poset recovery.
A calibration graph, rather than a calibration clique, with an exact edge-pattern compatibility frontier.
A selection-aware transport theorem for calibration moments from coordinate-aligned repeated sensors.

seed_details.destination_search: The full-pair anchor gives its edgewise diversity condition in Section 4.6, Assumption 2 and its identification conclusion in Theorem 3; DirectLiNGAM Lemmas 1--2 and Corollary 1 provide the closest single-path recursion, but neither paper states the partial-pair complete frontier.

literature_map: HeurtebiseEtAl2026LiMVAM is the flagship model anchor: Section 4.6, Assumption 2 imposes edgewise cross-view correlation diversity, and Theorem 3 identifies the partial order and all view-specific matrices under full pairing, with Assumption 3 adding total-order identification. The generic two-view theorem asks a different observation-regime question on the narrower component-aligned class and proves that any preassigned pair equals full calibration away from a proper algebraic set, without assuming their diversity condition. On the intersection with their assumptions, the two singleton conclusions agree as a restricted-domain consistency check. ShimizuEtAl2011DirectLiNGAM Section 3.1, Lemma 1 gives the residual-independence root criterion, Lemma 2 closes the model after one true-root removal, and Corollary 1 preserves the remaining order; it does not prove removed-set path independence or enumerate all compatible root sequences. JointLiNGAM, Chen et al., and Ghassami et al. share information across unpaired groups or domains through non-Gaussianity, latent population components, or heterogeneity rather than selected paired covariance blocks. HyttinenEberhardtHoyer2012Overlapping concerns experimental total effects. GuoPerkovic2021MinimalEffects, WienobstEtAl2023MECEnumeration, WangEtAl2023EquivalenceEnumeration, and AvisFukuda1996ReverseSearch provide quotient-enumeration templates but no local congruence for these numerical tuples. HauserBuhlmann2014ActiveLearning and LindgrenEtAl2018CostAware motivate only a separator analogy. GhoshalHonorio2018LinearSEM uses different precision-based gaps, while ChernozhukovHongTamer2007SetInference supplies the general inversion logic.
novelty_justification: The headline is the generic two-view theorem, not the fixed-order residual iff. For each wrong order, clearing positive principal-minor denominators gives an explicit polynomial, and a one-edge unequal-correlation parameter makes that polynomial nonzero. The finite product therefore defines a proper Lebesgue-null exceptional set, outside which any preassigned view pair yields the true order, the same singleton coefficient tuple as full calibration, and minimum admissible calibration size two. Heurtebise et al.'s Section 4.6, Assumption 2 and Theorem 3 instead use full pairing and edgewise diversity on a broader class; the comparison is restricted-domain and addresses a different observation regime. The equality witness \(P_{\mathrm{ex}}\) lies on the pair-specific exceptional set and shows that genericity cannot be replaced by an everywhere claim. Fixed-order completion and residual-witness hitting are supporting consequences. Removed-set path independence, complete compatible-order paths, explicit inference moduli, and the open output-sensitive quotient problem retain the original complete-frontier infrastructure.
message: Made generic sufficiency of any preassigned view pair the headline, defined its proper algebraic exceptional set and explicit nonvanishing witnesses, demoted definitional equivalences to supporting results, and propagated the change through inference, comparators, and scope.
